entities.summary:
Cercidas (b. 300 BCE, Megalopoli) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Megalopoli. He was a prominent figure in the development of Stoic philosophy, known for his work on the nature of the universe and the human condition. His ideas had a lasting impact on Western philosophy, influencing prominent thinkers such as Epictetus and Seneca.

Cercidas' contributions to Stoicism were largely lost to history until the 20th century, when scholars rediscovered his works and recognized his significant contributions to the development of the philosophy.

The legacy of Cercidas can be seen in the many philosophical schools and traditions that followed in his footsteps, including Neoplatonism and Epicureanism. His emphasis on reason, self-control, and indifference to external events helped shape the Stoic ideal of the individual, which has had a profound impact on Western culture and society.

Cercidas' philosophical ideas also had a lasting impact on the development of Western science, particularly in the areas of astronomy and mathematics. His observations on the movements of the stars and planets helped lay the foundations for later scientific discoveries.

In conclusion, Cercidas was a pivotal figure in the development of Stoic philosophy, whose ideas have had a lasting impact on Western culture and society. His contributions to the development of reason, self-control, and indifference to external events have helped shape the Stoic ideal of the individual, which continues to inspire and influence thinkers to this day.
